MajorDuties: You will be responsible for the direction and management of NUWC Division Newport's basic and applied research portfolio.
You will manage the In-House Laboratory Independent Research (ILIR) Program and the Naval Innovative Science and Engineering (NISE)/Section 219 (basic and applied) Research program.
You will support innovative research that is important and promising to the execution of NUWC Division Newport's undersea warfare mission.
You will develop a strong portfolio of basic and applied research projects through recognition of the fundamental scientific nature of the proposed work and its potential applicability to Navy needs.
You will lead the development of a cadre of active research scientists who can distill and extend results from worldwide research and apply results to problems of naval interest.
You will develop strategies for the Technology Focus Areas working directly with the research communities to establish long term goals and plans to achieve them.
You will collaborate and interface with the Technology Partnership Office in establishing pertinent Educational Partnership Agreements (EPA's) to foster educational outreach.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet at least one of the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Degree: A professional engineering degree from an ABET-accredited college or university; OR a degree with curriculum in differential and integral calculus, with additional courses in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics; or electronics; OR Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Substitution of Education/Experience: A combination of education and experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying professional engineering; and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: (a) professional registration, (b) evidence of successfully passing the Engineer-in-Training (EIT) examination; (c) successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified above; or (d) successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering technology or in an appropriate professional field, e.g., physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering provided that it included at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. (Note to Applicants: Please see the Qualifications & Education sections of this announcement for a link to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Individual Occupational Requirements. OPM guidance indicates that there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience. This training plan or experience must be well documented and provided at time of application.); OR 1360-Oceanography Series: A degree with major study of at least 24 semester hours in oceanography or a related discipline such as physics, meteorology, geophysics, mathematics, chemistry, engineering, geology, or biology, plus 20 additional semester hours in any combination of oceanography, physics, geophysics, chemistry, mathematics, meteorology, computer science, and engineering sciences; or a combination of of education and experience: coursework as shown above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. 1550-Computer Science Series: A degree in computer science; or a degree with at least 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Warfare Centers Personnel Demonstration Project. The ND-4 pay band encompasses positions equivalent to GS-12 and GS-13; the ND-5 pay band encompasses positions equivalent to GS-14 and GS-15. You will serve as the Torpedo Operational Software Lead Systems Engineer in the Undersea Warfare Weapons, Vehicles & Defensive Systems Dept.; Weapons Systems Division; Weapons Software & Computer Systems Branch (Code 8523) of the Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport.
Details.SubAgencyName: Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will be responsible for all phases of the software lifecycle from plan, develop, build, test, release, deliver, deploy, operate and maintain/monitor for all Torpedo Operational Software baselines/projects.

You will coordinate technical activities across a team comprised of industry, university labs and other government organizations; and provide the day-to-day technical direction and adjudication of technical issues necessary to execute tasking.
You will plan, organize, lead, direct and perform torpedo operational software development and systems engineering duties and assignments.
You will perform system engineering analyses to develop performance and interface specifications.
You will design and develop torpedo operational software-based solutions to meet torpedo system improvements/upgrades and/or resolve torpedo system problems.
You will generate and execute test plans to verify/validate torpedo operational software requirements and torpedo system requirements, conduct troubleshooting and evaluate proposed solutions.
You will perform tests in support of verification/validation of requirements.
You will integrate hardware and software.
You will document software designs in accordance with policies and procedures.
You will report and present results of analyses, designs, tests, integration, project status and issues (e.g., high-level briefs, correspondence, technical memorandums).
You will develop technical approaches for high level tasking, establish detailed plans, and estimate tasking costs and schedules.
You will establish technical performance metrics to assess product development progress against requirements.
You will develop necessary technical artifacts to conduct and present Systems Engineering Technical Reviews (SETRs).

You will provide recommendations to sponsors, program offices, fleet commands, Technical Warrant Holders, Warfare Centers, industry and academia on technical aspects of Torpedo Operational Software design and development efforts.
You will assist leadership in providing technical guidance and oversight of tasking required for successful execution of all Torpedo Operational Software development and sustainment efforts.
You will mentor engineering, scientific and technician personnel and ensure all tasking is performed with the appropriate level of technical rigor.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet at least one of the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Degree: A professional engineering degree from an ABET-accredited college or university; OR a degree with curriculum in differential and integral calculus, with additional courses in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics; or electronics; OR Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Substitution of Education/Experience: A combination of education and experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying professional engineering; and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: (a) professional registration, (b) evidence of successfully passing the Engineer-in-Training (EIT) examination; (c) successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified above; or (d) successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering technology or in an appropriate professional field, e.g., physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering provided that it included at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. (Note to Applicants: Please see the Qualifications & Education sections of this announcement for a link to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Individual Occupational Requirements. OPM guidance indicates that there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience. This training plan or experience must be well documented and provided at time of application.); OR 1550-Computer Science Series: A degree in computer science; or a degree with at least 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of these 30 semester hours must have been in a combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Warfare Centers Personnel Demonstration Project. The ND-4 pay band encompasses positions equivalent to GS-12 and GS-13; the ND-5 pay band encompasses positions equivalent to GS-14 and GS-15. You will serve as the Exterior Communications Deputy Technical Project Manager (DTPM) in the Technical Project Management Office (Code 349) of the Undersea Warfare Electromagnetic Systems Department of the Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport.
Details.SubAgencyName: Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will work with the Technical Project Manager (TPM) in the planning, budgeting, and managing the execution of all tasking for the External Communications, including Common Submarine Radio Room (CSRR), a major ACAT-II Acquisition program.
You will provide technical advice to top-level Navy management and technical personnel, other agencies, and private organizations.
You will serve on Navy, interagency, and technical society panels and committees of national or international scope.

You will support the TPM with the execution, direction, and success of major projects, systems development efforts, and research or technology initiatives which have great significance to the activity's and agency's needs.
You will be responsible for technical execution of NUWC Division Newport's CSRR Lead System Integrator role.
You will conduct engineering design, system integration, test and evaluation, logistics and maintenance of CSRR facilities in support of submarine modernization and new construction.

You will provide technical guidance to the NUWC Division Newport CSRR engineering team as well as formal review and approval of engineering drawings, to include Government Furnished Information to shipbuilder, as well as Engineering Change Requests.
You will support the TPM as the senior engineer for the cross-agency and contractor team that contributes to the CSRR.

You will serve as the chair of the CSRR System Engineering Team (SET), which has membership from PEO C4I, PEO SUB, SPAWAR ATLANTIC, Lockheed Martin, Fleet Representatives and various other contractor representatives.
You will provide technical guidance, as a recognized subject matter expert and expert consultant on all CSRR and Exterior Communications related technical matters.
You will support the TPM in the day-to-day technical oversight of the NUWC Division Newport CSRR technical team working in the area of submarine communications support and network systems.
You will collaborate with the TPM in planning for CSRR task execution by the engineering, technician and administrative team.
You will provide recommendations to the TPM regarding all External Communications efforts to ensure effective execution of the program and project objectives.
You will work with the TPM to conduct risk analysis and cost engineering estimations to seek engineering alternatives for problems encountered on the CSRR Program.
You will help define near term (yearly) and long term (FYDP+) program objectives, schedules and budget, and will support the development and negotiation of task spend plans with the sponsor.
You will help to staff and prioritize engineering and engineering support tasking within the Exterior Communications program.

You will review and validate the accuracy of financial reports, and will utilize engineering experience to develop schedule and technical progress reports for both internal (NUWC) and external (sponsor) stakeholders to support.
You will prepare briefs, action item responses, and technical white papers as required, and participate in routine and emergent staff and sponsor meetings.
You will act as the Exterior Communications program lead when the TPM is not present.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet at least one of the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Degree: A professional engineering degree from an ABET-accredited college or university; OR a degree with curriculum in differential and integral calculus, with additional courses in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics; or electronics; OR Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Substitution of Education/Experience: A combination of education and experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying professional engineering; and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: (a) professional registration, (b) evidence of successfully passing the Engineer-in-Training (EIT) examination; (c) successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified above; or (d) successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering technology or in an appropriate professional field, e.g., physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering provided that it included at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. (Note to Applicants: Please see the Qualifications & Education sections of this announcement for a link to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Individual Occupational Requirements. OPM guidance indicates that there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience. This training plan or experience must be well documented and provided at time of application.); OR 1310-Physics Series: A degree in physics; or a related degree that includes at least 24 semester hours in physics; or, a combination of education and experience demonstrated by coursework that is equivalent to a major in physics (at least 24 semester hours), plus appropriate experience or additional education; OR 1550-Computer Science Series: A degree in computer science or a degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of these 30 semester hours must have been in a combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus.

You will plan and assign work; provide performance development; recommend discipline, awards, promotions and other personnel actions; give personal advice and hear complaints.
You will negotiate with Center organizations regarding changes to the Division's service and advise Division Head on recommended changes.

You will work alongside the Division Head to establish priorities, determine methods to analyze and monitor costs, perform risk assessments, and devise plans and budgets to ensure sound fiscal management.
You will provide information to Branch supervisors and the Division Head in planning future requirements for the Center.
You will interface on a routine basis with Division Newport staff, Departments, customers and other organizations to accomplish objectives.
You will participate in recruiting events and help oversee resulting hiring actions.
You will prepare and execute strategic planning and assessment efforts on behalf of the Center.
You will be responsible for Continuous Process Improvement (CPI) and change management, and how to develop, socialize and execute technical/business solutions to support the Center?s mission.
You will provide expert advice/guidance on environmental and engineering aspects of projects, scientific concepts and results.
You will provide environmental and engineering plans, instructions, procedures, and scientific subject matter expertise to address Research, Development, Test and Evaluation requirements.
You will perform a key role in resolving complex issues that significantly affect various programs within Code 102.
You will apply expertise and experience in the areas across the multi-disciplines of Code 10 to develop business solutions to execute the command's technical engineering/scientific challenges.
You will develop strategies and advise Code 10 on how to best prepare the physical infrastructure, security, telecommunications and networks to support the mission of the Command.
You will serve as Code 10 Department Calibration Point-of-Contact.
You will coordinate all Code 10 strategic investments and serve as the Code 10 representative to review the technical Department's strategic investments.
You will review all proposed major changes to business processes and ensure they are based upon sound engineering/scientific practices and a solid business case analysis.
You will work with scientists and engineers across the Command on data calls, exercises, and demonstrations.
You will collectively work with the technical departments key personnel to ensure infrastructure and business processes support emerging mission requirements.
You will serve on the Warfare Center Facility Community of Practice.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: This is an interdisciplinary position and may be filled by a General Biological Scientist (0401-series), a Computer Engineer (0854-series), an Electronics Engineer (0855-series), an Oceanographer (1360-series), or a Mathematician (1520-series) depending upon the qualifications of the candidate. Applicants in positions with occupational series other than those listed (0401, 0854, 0855, 1360 and 1520) may apply; however, you must apply directly to the series listed in this vacancy that is most applicable to your qualifications. In addition to the Basic Requirements for this position, your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the ND-4 pay band (GS-12 and GS-13 equivalency) in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: As a professional engineer or scientist applying a wide range of systems engineering principles to manage and lead multiple, complex programs related to acoustic effect modeling on marine mammals. Examples of qualifying experience may include (1) planning and executing a range of projects from basic and applied research through complex analysis in support of the Navy's attainment of environmental approach for Fleet training exercises worldwide; (2) utilizing knowledge of U.S. environmental policy specific to marine mammal exposure to sound generated by navy exercises, acoustic propagation modeling, and marine species behavioral response. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Individual Occupational Requirements (IOR): General Natural Resources Management and Biological Sciences Series, 0401 All Professional Engineering Positions, 08XX Oceanography Series, 1360 Mathematics Series, 1520 Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Warfare Centers Personnel Demonstration Project. The ND-5 pay band encompasses positions equivalent to GS-14 and GS-15. You will serve as the Technical Project Manager (TPM) for the Marine Mammal Monitoring on Navy Ranges (M3R) Program as well as the Marine Species Modeling Team within the Program Management Office (Code 709) of the Ranges, Engineering, and Analysis Department of the Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport.
Details.SubAgencyName: Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as a recognized authority and expert consultant in the area of acoustic effect modeling on marine mammals.
You will regularly engage with the NUWC Division Newport Environmental Division, OPNAV N45, U.S. Fleet Forces (Atlantic and Pacific), and Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC).

You will work in close coordination with the Test and Evaluation Services and Marine Environmental Customer Advocate to negotiate tasking with the program office and with Division and Branch Heads to develop task statements and cost estimates.
You will develop research projects based on environmental permitting requirements.
You will conduct analyses and studies relating to marine mammal population, marine mammal response to sound emitted by naval ships, and marine mammal vocalization and behavior.
You will represent the activity and the command on high-level committees and groups with the responsibility and authority to defend the activity's position.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet at least one of the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: 0401-General Natural Resources Management and Biological Sciences Series: A degree in biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position; or a combination of education and experience: courses equivalent to a major, as shown above, plus appropriate experience or additional education; OR Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Degree: A professional engineering degree from an ABET-accredited college or university; OR a degree with curriculum in differential and integral calculus, with additional courses in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics; or electronics; OR Professional Engineering Series (08XX) - Substitution of Education/Experience: A combination of education and experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying professional engineering; and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: (a) professional registration, (b) evidence of successfully passing the Engineer-in-Training (EIT) examination; (c) successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified above; or (d) successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering technology or in an appropriate professional field, e.g., physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering provided that it included at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. (Note to Applicants: Please see the Qualifications & Education sections of this announcement for a link to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Individual Occupational Requirements. OPM guidance indicates that there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience. This training plan or experience must be well documented and provided at time of application.); OR 1360-Oceanography Series: A degree with major study of at least 24 semester hours in oceanography or a related discipline such as physics, meteorology, geophysics, mathematics, chemistry, engineering, geology, or biology, plus 20 additional semester hours in any combination of oceanography, physics, geophysics, chemistry, mathematics, meteorology, computer science, and engineering sciences; or a combination of education and experience -- course work as shown above, plus appropriate experience or additional education; OR 1520-Mathematics Series: A degree in mathematics; or a combination of education and experience - courses equivalent to a major in mathematics (including at least 24 semester hours in mathematics), plus appropriate experience or additional education. The total coursework described above must have included differential and integral calculus and, in addition, four advanced mathematics courses requiring calculus or equivalent mathematics courses as a prerequisite.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Technical Project Manager in the USW Electromagnetic Systems Department of NAVUNSEAWARCENDIV NEWPORT RI. If selected, you will serve as the USW Electromagnetic Maneuver Warfare (EMW) Advanced Technology Development (ATD) Deputy Technical Project Manager (DTPM). This position is part of the Warfare Centers Personnel Demonstration Project. ND-05 is equivalent to GS-14/15.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will work with the Technical Project Manager (TPM) in the planning, budgeting, scheduling and tracking the execution of all tasking assignments for the program.

You will conduct analysis of alternatives to identify solutions and engineering alternatives to address emergent threats, requirements, and desired capabilities for a variety of submarine, surface, air, and unmanned vehicle programs and platforms.
You will act as a collaborator with the TPM for the development of EMW technology roadmaps to ensure leveraging and development efforts address emergent threats and future required capabilities.
You will serve as an expert in the required EMW systems and missions of a variety of submarine, surface, air, and unmanned vehicles.

You will utilize knowledge of design of RF systems, Digital Receivers, RF Photonics, Open Systems Architectures, and the national SIGINT Production Chain to enable improved Electronic Warfare Systems and Communication Systems.
You will help define near term (yearly) program objectives, schedules and budget, and shall develop task plans and review these with the TPM and program office PAPM prior to final submission.
You will review and validate the accuracy of financial reports.

You will utilize engineering experience to develop and schedule technical progress reports for both internal and external customers to support monthly reporting; Quarterly Financial Reviews and Program Reviews; and ad-hoc status reviews.
You will prepare briefs, action item responses, and technical white papers as required.
You will, when needed, lead routine and emergent staff and sponsor meetings and will act as the EMW ATD program technical lead when the TPM is not present.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: FOR THE 0830/0854/0855 - Professional Engineering Series: A. Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR B. Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR C. Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR D. Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR E, Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. FOR THE 1310 - Physics Series: A degree in physics; or related degree that includes at least 24 semester hours in physics; or, a combination of education and experience demonstrated by coursework that is equivalent to a major in physics (at least 24 semester hours), plus appropriate experience or additional education. FOR THE 1550 - Computer Science Series: A degree in computer science or degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours were in a combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as the Hull Sensor Systems Program Lead Systems Engineer (LSE) working within FLEET SENSORS & CABLES ENG BR in the SENSORS & ARRAYS DIVISION in the SENSORS & SONAR SYSTEMS DEPARTMENT for NAVUNSEAWARCENDIV NEWPORT RI. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. MajorDuties: You will be responsible for technical oversight of the procurement, restoration, and lifecycle support activities of a diverse product line of underwater sensors.
You will apply lead system engineering principles in resolving sensor/SONAR system performance deficiencies.

You will support the Hull Sensor Systems Program Technical Program Manager (TPM), Code 15 Chief Engineer (CHENG) and the transducer/sensor/array development, acquisition, and in-service support programs of NAVSEA PMS401 and PMS450.
You will perform as the lead technical expert for the Hull Sensors program.

You will provide technical stewardship by implementing robust systems engineering processes across all sensor products to ensure system performance requirements are being met and not negatively impacted by proposed engineering changes.
You will provide periodic technical status reports/presentations detailing the efforts underway to resolve project specific issues to all levels of civilian and military personnel.
You will lead teams in the development of technical point papers, analyses, documents, and/or reports to address technical issues.
You will provide TDA technical leadership for all sensor development/production/restoration contracts.
You will perform as resident technical expert in hull sensor system designs to senior level forums.
You will mentor junior personnel in performing in an Lead Systems Engineer role.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: For the 08XX, Professional Engineering Series: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. For the 1550, Professional Computer Science Series: A bachelor's degree in computer science. OR A bachelor's or higher degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must be in a combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. MajorDuties: You will monitor weather patterns and issue weather forecasts for authorized customer in the Fleet Weather Center, Norfolk (FWC-N) area of responsibility.
You will conduct research, case studies, and coordinate with other scientists to improve both short-range forecasts and long-range forecasts.
You will stand watch as an OTSR ship officer and use optimum route planning tools for ocean voyage transits by choosing the least-time route that avoids meteorological and sea state hazards.
You will screen subordinate locally produced forecasts, prognostic charts, and warning during normal working hours.
You will act as the Senior Meteorologist during their absence.
You will supervise three civilian watch team personnel on a 24/7 rotating watch bill.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual.Applicants must possess the following Basic Requirements: Degree: meteorology, atmospheric science, or other natural science major that included: At least 24 semester (36 quarter) hours of credit in meteorology/atmospheric science including a minimum of: Six semester hours of atmospheric dynamics and thermodynamics;* Six semester hours of analysis and prediction of weather systems (synoptic/mesoscale); Three semester hours of physical meteorology; and Two semester hours of remote sensing of the atmosphere and/or instrumentation. Six semester hours of physics, with at least one course that includes laboratory sessions.* Three semester hours of ordinary differential equations.* At least nine semester hours of course work appropriate for a physical science major in any combination of three or more of the following: physical hydrology, statistics, chemistry, physical oceanography, physical climatology, radiative transfer, aeronomy, advanced thermodynamics, advanced electricity and magnetism, light and optics, and computer science. * There is a prerequisite or corequisite of calculus for course work in atmospheric dynamics and thermodynamics, physics, and differential equations. Calculus courses must be appropriate for a physical science major. or Combination of education and experience -- course work as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. A copy of School Transcripts must be provided to verify basic education requirements.

MajorDuties: You will serve as the expert authority in the field of hull, mechanical and electrical machinery research and development, machinery commonality, condition based logistics, technical data utilization, ship integrity and shock resilience.

You will manage and oversee complex multi-disciplinary research and development on engineering programs involving applied research and development in machinery systems and assignments for future investments.

You will coordinate and integrate technical efforts with requirements and potential solutions with the experts in the Division, other government agencies, the fleet, Naval Sea Systems Command, Office of Naval Research, and academia.

You will be responsible for supporting the research and innovation on marine machinery systems, including supporting and strengthening technology development and transition across various organizations.

You will provide overall, third level, technical and managerial direction for a major department within the Division and provide authoritative technical advice and recommendations on matters related to research and development.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following Basic Requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: For 0801 Professional Engineering Series: A. Degree: Engineering. Successful completion of a bachelor's or higher engineering degree from an accredited college or university. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. -or- B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: (I) Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions; or (II) Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico; or (III) Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A; or (IV) Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.) OR For 1301 General Physical Sciences Series: Successful completion of a degree in physical science, engineering, or mathematics that includes 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics; or, a combination of education and experience in one of the above majors that includes at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. For 1501 Mathematics Series: Successful completion of a degree in mathematics, statistics, or actuarial science; or a combination of education and experience demonstrated by coursework that is equivalent to a major in mathematics, statistics, or actuarial science (at least 24 semester hours), plus appropriate experience or additional education. An advanced degree of Master's or Ph.D. in one of the educational fields listed above is highly desirable.

Details.SubAgencyName: Naval Research Laboratory (NRL)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as the Head of the Electro-Optic and Infrared (EO/IR) Concepts Section supervising five (5) employees.
You will manage the financial budget of the EO/IR Concepts Section.
You will conduct research and development on EO/IR Electronic Warfare (EW) technologies and applications.
You will initiate and direct laser countermeasure (DIRCM) and Directed Energy (DE) programs to develop concepts, techniques, and devices to defeat EO/IR, Radio Frequency (RF), and hybrid programs.
You will conduct research and development (R and D) on the interaction of lasers and threat guidance units and the performance impact to the threat.
You will conduct Research and Development on novel optical augmentation (OA) techniques.
You will develop brassboard devices and systems from the conducted research.
You will serve as Principle Investigator (PI) of multiple technology-based Research and Development programs for various Navy Sponsors and participate in all aspects of the program.
You will prepare memoranda, financial and technical reports, and publications.
You will conduct Research and Development on novel Optical Augmentation (OA) techniques.
Details.Education: Basic Requirement - Series: 1310: Degree: physics; or related degree that included at least 24 semester hours in physics. OR Combination of education and experience -- courses equivalent to a major in physics totaling at least 24 semester hours, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In either option above, the courses must have included a fundamental course in general physics and, in addition, courses in any two of the following: electricity and magnetism, heat, light, mechanics, modern physics, and sound. For more information: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/1300/physics-series-1310/ Series: 0855: A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1 , or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.) Note: An applicant who meets the basic requirements as specified in A or B above, except as noted under B.1., may qualify for positions in any branch of engineering unless selective factors indicate otherwise. For more information: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0800/files/all-professional-engineering-positions-0800.pdf

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Providing natural/marine resource and environmental planning management to include program development, project execution/delivery of products and services, technical support, and cross organization training coordination; 2) Conducting regulatory consultations/permitting to support in-water construction projects along industrialized waterfronts; 3) Implementing and enforcing DoD, DON, OPNAV, and CNIC policy and guidance related to natural/marine resources, environmental planning, and shore installation management; 4) Providing environmental expertise on issues related to natural/marine resources and NEPA; 5) Planning, programming, budgeting, and executing environmental requirements; and 6) Communicating complex and sometimes controversial ideas, and displaying the ability to relay scientific information to the public and regulatory agencies in a logical and easy to understand format. MajorDuties: You will review and lead or participate in the development of NEPA documentation, including completion of regulatory consultations and permitting necessary for SIOP program execution.
You will develop plans of accomplishment, including schedules and acquisition plans related to SIOP facilities projects requiring natural/marine resource and environmental planning support.

You will obtain natural/marine resource consultation concurrences and permits with outside federal and state agencies to ensure that the consultation/permitting process does not delay SIOP construction schedules.

You will assist in overseeing the overall long-range planning, direction, and timely execution of SIOP projects or initiatives related to natural/marine resource and environmental planning requirements.
You will serve as a senior functional specialist and technical expert for natural/marine resource matters specific to the assigned shipyard?s SIOP program.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a TECHNICAL PROJECT MANAGER in the SIGNATURE TRAINERS BRANCH of the SIGNATURES FLEET SYSTEMS DIVISION in the SIGNATURES DEPARTMENT of CARDEROCK DIV NS. This position is equivalent to the GS-14/15 level.
Details.SubAgencyName: NAVAL SURFACE WARFARE CENTER CARDEROCK
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will be responsible for Submarine Trainer development in the Fleet Signatures Systems Division of the Signatures Department.
You will be responsible for development, integration, implementation, delivery and maintenance of all Submarine Trainer systems, and for new system variants as they enter the Fleet.
You will manage system development, integration, implementation, delivery, support, oversight, maintenance and engineering tasking for Submarine Trainer systems.
You will build in maximum commonality to leverage capability, hardware design and software modules across systems to lower overall project cost.
You will coordinate with program sponsors and senior Fleet personnel regarding financial support and budget-related issues for all Submarine Trainer systems as they are developed.
You will play a key role in developing Statements of Work for new contracts to support Signature Trainer systems.

You will serve as the senior technical interface between Submarine Trainer development team members, other technical groups at NSWCCD, Fleet representatives, program offices, industry experts, and experts at other Navy labs.
You will make recommendations and guides research into advancing technologies and novel engineering approaches for Submarine Training systems.

You will provide technical expertise and management required to support multiple major projects and sponsors while coordinating and leveraging common development baselines to provide cost-effective Submarine Trainer systems for the Navy.
You will make presentations, prepare technical reports/papers, support program technical reviews and financial reviews.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: For the 08XX, Professional Engineering Series: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. For the 1310, Physics Series: Successful completion of a bachelor's degree or higher physics or related degree that included at least 24 semester hours in physics. Courses must have included a fundamental course in general physics and, in addition, course in any of two of the following: electricity and magnetism, heat, light, mechanics, modern physics, and sound. OR Successful completion of a combination of education and experience with courses equivalent to a major in physics totaling at least 24 semester hours, plus appropriate experience or additional education. Courses must have included a fundamental course in general physics and, in addition, course in any of two of the following: electricity and magnetism, heat, light, mechanics, modern physics, and sound. For the 1550, Computer Science Series: Successful completion of a bachelor's degree or higher in computer science. OR Successful completion of a bachelor's or higher degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of my 30 semester hours were in a combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a MANAGER (BRANCH HEAD) in the SIGNATURE, CONTROL ANALYSIS & SUSCEPTIBILITY BRANCH of the UNDERWATER ELECTROMAGNETIC (UEM) SIGNATURES & TECHNOLOGY DIVISION in the SIGNATURES DEPARTMENT of CARDEROCK DIV NS. This position is equivalent to the GS-14/15 level.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will provide technical leadership in underwater electromagnetic (UEM) signatures and silencing, to include influencing projects, proposals, and direction of work.
You will provides technical direction and oversight of UEM signatures technology and silencing system research, development, design, testing, acquisition support, and in-service engineering.
You will advocate for commonality, perform critical assessments, identify issues, provide guidance to achieve solutions, and determining risk to meeting objectives.

You will conduct susceptibility assessments for all Navy platforms from underwater influence mines, undersea surveillance systems, and airborne sensor systems that detect and actuate on a target?s electromagnetic field emissions
You will interface with sponsors, the Fleet, and MSF personnel, providing UEM signature control, analysis, and susceptibility expertise.
You will develop strategies for the Branch?s future direction in line with Division and Department goals.
You will manage branch financial, physical, and human resources, to include providing mentorship and coaching to branch employees.
You will provide program oversight for Sponsors and Division management.
You will oversee the routine administrative operations of the Branch.
You will support NAVSEA Engineering and Technical Authority and technical warrant holders in Underwater Electromagnetic Signatures and Susceptibility.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: For the 08XX, Professional Engineering Series: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. For the 1310, Physics Series: Successful completion of a bachelor's degree or higher in physics; or related degree that included at least 24 semester hours in physics. Courses must have included a fundamental course in general physics and, in addition, courses in any two of the following: electricity and magnetism, heat, light, mechanics, modern physics, and sound. OR Successful completion of a combination of education and experience -- courses equivalent to a major in physics totaling at least 24 semester hours, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Professional and Scientific Positions and the Individual Occupational Requirements (IOR) for the GS-1515 Operations Research Series. BASIC REQUREMENT OR INDIVIDUAL REQUIREMENT: GS-1515: A Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in operations research; or at least 24 semester hours in a combination of operations research, mathematics, probability, statistics, mathematical logic, science, or subject-matter courses requiring substantial competence in college-level mathematics or statistics. At least 3 of the 24 semester hours must have been in calculus. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts with your application. EVALUATION OF EDUCATION: The primary requirement of operations research work is competence in the rigorous methods of scientific inquiry and analysis rather than in the subject matter of the problem. Therefore, applicants should have sufficient knowledge of applied mathematics to understand and use the fundamental concepts and techniques of operations research methods of analysis. In addition, some positions may require knowledge of a specific subject area. Courses acceptable for qualifying for operations research positions may have been taken in departments other than Operations Research, e.g., Engineering (usually Industrial Engineering), Science, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or Management Science. AND SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must meet the basic requirements for the GS-1515-12 and have at least one (1) year of specialized experience to the GS-11 (or higher) grade level or equivalent pay system (may have been obtained in the Federal service, military, or private sector). Specialized experience includes knowledge of weapons systems and a wide range of methods and techniques used in operations research studies to recommend those suitable for producing explicit findings and discriminating evaluations. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts with your application. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-11 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-12 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Expert knowledge of the Electronic Warfare (EW) development area. Knowledge will include, but not limited to, EW principles (radar theory, IR theory, basic electronic theory, microwaves), EW equipment (radar warning receivers, electronic countermeasures pods, countermeasures dispensing systems, radar systems, and radio systems), EW tactics, and EW sources. 2. Knowledge of Advanced Threats to include, but not limited to, aircraft, airborne missiles, ground based missiles, integrated air defense systems, and anti-aircraft artillery systems. 3. Knowledge of weapons systems and a wide range of methods and techniques used in operations research studies and analytical abilities. 4. Knowledge of and experience in applying learning theory and the principles practices, and techniques of instruction. 5. Knowledge of instructional design and material development. 6. In-depth knowledge of technical writing/editing principles. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
